newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer buys Pharmacia animal drug unit.
newsitem.headline: Bayer buys Pharmacia animal drug unit.

text.p: Germany's Bayer AG said on Monday that it has signed a deal with a unit of U.S. pharmaceuticals company Pharmacia & Upjohn to acquire its animal health vaccines business.
Terms of the agreement were not released.
Bayer said the deal covers manufacturing and research facilities in Worthington, Minnesota, and a manufacturing plant in Omaha, Nebraska, along with associated licensed products.
The deal also covers intellectual property and diagnostic services.
Bayer said the acquisition represented another step in the growth of its animal health business in the United States, where it is aiming for a 10 percent market share by 2000.
The animal healthcare business group reported worldwide sales in 1996 of almost 1.3 billion marks ($830 million), Bayer said.
